## FIRST RULE

After your first successful edit_file or write_file, your very next action
is submit_patch. Then continue working and call submit_patch again after
every further change. submit_patch is free — it does not count against your
tool-call budget. If you time out, only your last submitted patch is scored.

## Scratch files

Write any reproduction or debugging script to /tmp, never inside /workspace.
Everything left in /workspace becomes part of your submitted patch.
Do not modify test files, conftest.py or pytest.ini — those changes are
stripped before grading, so editing them wastes tool calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

Start with grep:
  run_command("grep -rn '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")
Read files only after grep has narrowed the candidates. Keep read_file
ranges tight — each call returns at most 150 lines and consumes context
you will need later.

class Segment(NamedTuple):

    are ultimately converted in to strings to be written to the terminal.

        control (Tuple[ControlCode], optional): Optional sequence of control codes.

    text: str
    style: Optional[Style] = None
    control: Optional[Sequence[ControlCode]] = None

    @property
    def cell_length(self) -> int:
        """The number of terminal cells required to display self.text.

        Returns:
            int: A number of cells.
        """
        text, _style, control = self
        return 0 if control else cell_len(text)

    def __rich_repr__(self) -> Result:
        yield self.text
        if self.control is None:
            if self.style is not None:
                yield self.style
        else:
            yield self.style
            yield self.control

    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
        """Check if the segment contains text."""
        return bool(self.text)

    @property
    def is_control(self) -> bool:
        """Check if the segment contains control codes."""

class Segments:
    """A simple renderable to render an iterable of segments. This class may be useful if
    you want to print segments outside of a __rich_console__ method.

    Args:
        segments (Iterable[Segment]): An iterable of segments.
        new_lines (bool, optional): Add new lines between segments. Defaults to False.
    """

    def __init__(self, segments: Iterable[Segment], new_lines: bool = False) -> None:
        self.segments = list(segments)
        self.new_lines = new_lines

    def __rich_console__(
        self, console: "Console", options: "ConsoleOptions"
    ) -> "RenderResult":
        if self.new_lines:
            line = Segment.line()
            for segment in self.segments:
                yield segment
                yield line
        else:
            yield from self.segments


class SegmentLines:
    def __init__(self, lines: Iterable[List[Segment]], new_lines: bool = False) -> None:
        """A simple renderable containing a number of lines of segments. May be used as an intermediate
        in rendering process.

        Args:
            lines (Iterable[List[Segment]]): Lists of segments forming lines.
            new_lines (bool, optional): Insert new lines after each line. Defaults to False.
        """
        self.lines = list(lines)
        self.new_lines = new_lines

    def __rich_console__(
        self, console: "Console", options: "ConsoleOptions"
    ) -> "RenderResult":
        if self.new_lines:
            new_line = Segment.line()
            for line in self.lines:
                yield from line
                yield new_line
        else:
            for line in self.lines:
                yield from line
